experiment: Watchdog G3 selection and held-out evaluation
status_at_freeze: protocol frozen before this pilot was executed; no claim of retrospective preregistration
question: Does selecting the largest absolute cohort statistic inflate nominal rejection when evaluation reuses the search observations, compared with independent held-out evaluation?

generator.description: Independent cohorts of iid Normal(mu,1) observations. Generate exact Gaussian sufficient statistics for three independent blocks A, B, C of n observations; individual observations are not materialized. The raw data are the block z statistics, not patient data.
generator.normal_algorithm: Box-Muller, two math functions and two uniform draws per generated pair
generator.uniform_algorithm: Python random.Random.random using per-trial integer seed SHA256 of g3-v1|root_seed|scenario|trial interpreted as big-endian

design.cohorts: disjoint and independent; budgets use prefixes of the same 20 cohorts
design.selection: largest absolute z; lowest index wins exact ties
design.multiplicity: Nominal methods apply alpha to one selected p value. Bonferroni methods apply alpha/m to selected search p. Held-out evaluation tests exactly one frozen cohort once at alpha; no selection among held-out results.
comparisons: Fixed total observations and search budget: explore_200 vs confirm_100 (2*n*m observations each).
Equal evaluation sample size: explore_100 vs confirm_100 (different total observations).
Equal evaluation sample size sensitivity: explore_200 vs confirm_200 (2*n*m versus 3*n*m).
No-search cohort 0 is preselected; in one_signal it is an oracle/favorable fixed target, not blind discovery.
All cohorts are generated for comparability; sample_cost is the observation budget logically consumed by the method, not Python runtime.

metrics.unit: one independent trial; never individual cohort tests as the denominator
metrics.denominator: 5000 trials per scenario, budget and method; budgets and methods share draws and are paired
metrics.null: any rejection = type-I error; no claim that nominal alpha controls family error after reuse
one_signal: true discovery = selected cohort 0 and rejection
false discovery = selected null cohort and rejection
metrics.intervals: Marginal 95% Wilson score intervals for Bernoulli rates; Monte Carlo uncertainty, not scientific population intervals; no simultaneous coverage or significance claim across tables. Seed is fixed, intervals describe hypothetical repetitions.
metrics.comparisons: paired rejection-rate differences, standard error from within-trial {-1,0,1} differences and normal 95% interval; descriptive, not independent-arm intervals
metrics.effect_bias: mean selected estimated effect; report interpretation because two-sided selection can choose either sign

checks.analytic_fixed_signal_power: P(|N(mu*sqrt(n),1)| > Phi^-1(1-alpha/2)) via erfc and statistics.NormalDist
checks.monte_carlo_tolerance: abs(observed-expected) <= 5*sqrt(expected*(1-expected)/trials); diagnostic only, all discrepancies retained
checks.determinism: rerun into a new output directory, compare raw and summary artifact SHA256 byte for byte

limitations: Synthetic independent Gaussian disjoint cohorts only. Overlapping subgroup searches, unknown variance, adaptive stopping and general replication are out of scope.
Confirmation depends on real isolation of holdout data, one frozen selection and no repeated reuse.
This pilot does not change locked JH16 or constitute clinical evidence.
Protocol timestamp and hash are a local pre-run record, not an external registration.
